headline: High risk of data leakage and capability conflict: aci can egress to third-party services while awesome-selfhosted is a non-runnable reference list with no isolation or controls.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: aci can ingest content via direct function calls or MCP, so if a user manually copies awesome-selfhosted content into aci, prompt injection is possible. awesome-selfhosted is not runnable and exposes no shared channel by default, so the bridge is manual and the blast radius is limited.
conditions: IF the operator copies untrusted text from awesome-selfhosted into aci prompts or MCP inputs, injection becomes plausible.
IF a shared filesystem or clipboard bridge is introduced, the risk increases beyond manual copy-paste.
mitigations: Use a strict copy-paste policy: paste only vetted excerpts into aci.
Wrap pasted content in quotes and ask aci to summarize, not execute instructions.
Disable any MCP connector that ingests raw markdown or HTML.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to imported notes before aci reads them.

B_data_leakage.rationale: aci touches CRM, email, calendar, and support data and has broad network egress, so it can leak sensitive data if fed into external services. awesome-selfhosted is only a static knowledge list, so it is not itself a data source, but pairing it with aci still creates a default path for sensitive context to leave the local environment.
conditions: IF CRM or email content is entered into aci and then sent to external APIs, leakage occurs.
IF the operator stores sensitive notes from aci in a shared workspace, those notes can be exposed through downstream integrations.
mitigations: Avoid placing secrets or customer data into aci prompts.
Restrict aci integrations to non-sensitive test accounts.
Review outbound API destinations before enabling them.
Turn off automatic sync for email and CRM connectors.
requires-engineering: segregate sensitive and non-sensitive workspaces.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: aci supports multiple instances and can write through integrations, but awesome-selfhosted is not runnable and has no write surfaces. There is no documented shared mutable resource between them, so direct write-write conflict is unlikely unless the operator adds one.
conditions: IF the operator connects aci to a shared CRM, sheet, or notes backend also edited elsewhere, conflicts can arise.
IF a shared filesystem or git workspace is added, concurrent edits become possible.
mitigations: Keep awesome-selfhosted read-only.
Use one writer per external system.
Enable version history on shared documents.
Pause one aci instance before bulk edits.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: awesome-selfhosted is a reference list, not an action-taking agent, so it is unlikely to blindly execute aci output. aci can produce operational content for email, CRM, and calendar, but without a downstream autonomous executor in the pair, cascading errors are limited to bad recommendations rather than automatic actions.
conditions: IF the operator uses aci output as authoritative input to a separate automation, errors can cascade.
IF awesome-selfhosted-derived recommendations are copied into aci without verification, misinformation can propagate.
mitigations: Require human review before sending emails or CRM updates.
Cross-check aci outputs against source records.
Use draft mode for all outbound actions.
Keep a changelog of copied recommendations.
requires-engineering: add validation rules before any write action.

E_compliance.rationale: aci handles email, CRM, and customer support data, which can carry privacy obligations, while awesome-selfhosted is a public self-hosted software index with no data residency or retention controls. The pair does not itself create a documented residency mismatch, but aci’s handling of regulated data warrants basic compliance review.
conditions: IF regulated customer data is entered into aci, retention and access policies must be checked.
IF the operator exports aci data into a jurisdiction with stricter rules, compliance obligations change.
mitigations: Classify data before entering it into aci.
Avoid storing regulated data in notes or prompts.
Document retention settings for connected services.
Review vendor DPAs for external integrations.
requires-engineering: implement residency and retention controls.
